solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Growth of pack animal?

parts.note: a pack of people or hounds is a gang
the lion is the big cat, an animal

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what a pack animal grows into, or what grows on one.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'pack animal' is not a mule or donkey but a lion running with a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a cyst-like swelling on a tendon, so medically a growth.

clue.text: Bow to topless female in secret…

parts.note: a bow is an arc, a curved shape

indicators.note: a word without its top loses its first letter

parts.note: Jane is a female name standing for any woman

explanation.surface: A bow made to a lady wearing nothing up top, done on the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the J from JANE, leaving ANE; the ellipsis links this clue to the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane knowledge is known only to a few initiates, mysterious and hidden.

clue.text: …Fellers! Reportedly that's the form

indicators.note: reported speech is heard rather than read, so the word for fellers is spoken

parts.note: fellers, chaps, are guys

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: an exclamation at the men, and a remark that this is how things are done.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward appearance or shape something takes.

clue.text: Concentrate when dealing with decimals if unknown quantity

parts.note: decimals are worked in tens, giving the phrase in tens
y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A maths lesson: working in base ten when one quantity is unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; 'dealing with decimals' gives the two words IN TENS run together.
explanation.definitionFit: To concentrate something is to make it stronger or more intense, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Gene mostly gets to play for the reserves

indicators.note: letters put into play are moved around freely
most of the word means its final letter goes

parts.note: the man's name taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Gene usually gets a game only for the reserve team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims GENE to GEN; with GETS that makes the letters to rearrange. 'reserves' looks like the second team, but here it means savings.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is money put aside as savings for the future.

clue.text: Stick with setter, say? That's dim!

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: to stick something is to glue it; the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A cheeky aside: if you side with the setter, you must be dim.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and dim both describe poorly lit, dark surroundings.

clue.text: German on consortium brought up sticky matter

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up reads it from the bottom

parts.note: a pool is a combined group sharing resources

explanation.surface: A German raises some sticky issue at a business consortium meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloop is informal for any thick, sticky, semi-liquid substance.

clue.text: Bilbo got active, mysteriously independent backing

indicators.note: something done mysteriously happens in a jumbled, unexplained way

parts.note: the hobbit's name taken as written
taken as written
A is the grammar abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: Bilbo Baggins sprang into action in a mysterious way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'active' gives A, an abbreviation used in grammar for the active voice.
explanation.definitionFit: An obbligato is a musical accompaniment line that is essential and stands as a distinct part of the piece.

clue.text: Accident across square on base of statue creates deformity

indicators.note: one word set across another straddles it, so it holds the other inside

parts.note: an accident is a mishap

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the last letter

explanation.surface: A mishap in a town square leaves a statue's plinth damaged and misshapen.
explanation.definitionFit: A misshape is a deformed or badly formed shape, a malformation.

clue.text: Handwriting he's extracted from broken pitchers

indicators.note: broken items are in pieces, so the remaining letters are rearranged
taking letters out of a word removes them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man digs some old handwriting out of the shards of smashed jugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he's' reads as 'he is'. Removing HE from PITCHERS leaves PITCRS for 'broken' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Script is handwriting, as opposed to print.

clue.text: Putting no books in central libraries is monstrous arrogance

indicators.note: in means the pieces are set inside the hidden letters
the central stretch of the run of words gives a run of letters from inside it

parts.note: taken as written
B is short for book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: A complaint that removing books from city-centre libraries is outrageous arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monstrous' looks like part of the definition, but 'central' takes the middle four letters of the run of three words; 'Putting ... in' sets the pieces inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Snobbism is snobbery, a superior and arrogant attitude to others.

clue.text: Network takes first of emissaries for Thailand captive

indicators.note: the word takes one letter in place of another, swapping them

parts.note: the internet is the worldwide computer network
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A news network carries a report on envoys sent to Thailand to plead for a captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... for' means E replaces T: the final T of INTERNET.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is a person confined, often in wartime, a kind of prisoner.

clue.text: Difficult situation from former engagement

definitions.meaning: in old usage to ... one's troth was to pledge to marry, so a ... was a betrothal

explanation.surface: A tricky situation arising from a past betrothal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plight means a predicament, and archaically a pledge, especially of marriage.

clue.text: Risking a fight — as the cowboy was with his horse?

definitions.meaning: quick to shoot and so likely to start trouble

definitions.text: as the cowboy was with his horse?
definitions.meaning: Trigger was the cowboy Roy Rogers's horse, so he was happy with Trigger

explanation.surface: A cowboy who goes looking for trouble, and is pleased with his horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Rogers was a singing cowboy of American films whose horse was called Trigger.
explanation.definitionFit: Being trigger-happy means being too ready to fire or to start a confrontation.

clue.text: Traveller about to blunder — turn away, he's a dangerous man!

indicators.note: about means going around something
sent away means taken out

parts.note: a tourist is a traveller
a U-turn makes U stand for turn
to blunder is to err

explanation.surface: A warning to a traveller about to make a mistake: turn back, this man is dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn away' sends the U out of TOURIST, leaving TORIST, which goes 'about' ERR.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrorist uses violence to intimidate, a man who is a danger to others.

clue.text: Pieces by strolling players resurfacing, maybe?

definitions.meaning: touring players are on the road

explanation.surface: Plays by a touring company coming back into fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resurfacing' looks like a revival of the plays; 'maybe' marks it as one example of work on a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadworks are repairs carried out on a road, such as laying a new surface.

clue.text: Multi-layered and specialised help with tyre

indicators.note: made specialised means adapted or altered, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tyre made of several layers, with expert help on hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something three-ply has three layers or strands, so it is layered.

clue.text: Initially rare tracheotomy operation bears little fruit

indicators.note: operating on the letters works them into new order
the first letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rare windpipe operation has produced a small, unexpected result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operation' looks like part of the medical story, but it signals the rearrangement of R plus TRACHEOTOMY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry tomato is a small variety of tomato, botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Grandpa's right, perhaps, being a man of experience

parts.note: a grandpa is an old man, so the word is old
the right is one example of a hand

explanation.surface: Grandpa turns out to be right, since he has years of experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' reads as correct, but with 'perhaps' it is the right hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hand is a veteran, someone with long practice at something.

clue.text: Radical wheeze a Lothario conceals

indicators.note: the words hold a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A seducer hides some extreme scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is a fanatic, someone with extreme views.

clue.text: Margaret's determined to be ruined

parts.note: Peg is a pet form of Margaret
to be out to do something is to be determined

explanation.surface: Margaret is set on bringing about her own ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Margaret's' stands for 'Margaret is', and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To peg out is to collapse, die or give up, so to be finished or ruined.

clue.text: Kick around gym in hat

indicators.note: one word put around another holds it inside

parts.note: to toe a ball is to kick it
PE, physical education, is gym

explanation.surface: Kicking a hat around the school gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A topee is a lightweight sun helmet once worn in the tropics.

clue.text: Fresh tint about East River by early dawn

indicators.note: about means going around something

parts.note: to tint is to dye
the Wye is a river on the England-Wales border

indicators.note: early means the first letter

explanation.surface: An early-morning view of a river in the east, coloured by the first light.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy-eyed means innocent or naive, like something fresh and youthful.

clue.text: Who among the French avoids calm study?

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out

parts.note: quietude is calm or stillness
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: Asking which French student skips quiet study time.
explanation.definitionFit: An etude is a musical study, a piece written to practise a technique.

clue.text: Processed veg — as regularly pre-war?

parts.note: the alternate letters of pre-war, split out of the word, are p, e, a

explanation.surface: Wartime-style processed vegetables, as they used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking alternate letters of PRE-WAR splits it and leaves P, E, A, so the clue describes a pea split out of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Split peas are dried peas with the halves separated, a processed vegetable.

clue.text: Currency problem when short of time

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so it is removed

parts.note: a problem is trouble

explanation.surface: Money problems arise when time runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is Russia's unit of currency.

clue.text: Girl's termly resolution

indicators.note: resolving something sorts it out, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl's promise for the new term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' looks like a pledge but signals the rearrangement; 'Girl's' is 'Girl is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Placed the accent on returning courses

indicators.note: a returning word goes back, so it is read from the end

parts.note: to place an accent on a syllable is to stress it

explanation.surface: Someone emphasised the point about the sweet courses.
explanation.definitionFit: Desserts are the sweet courses at the end of a meal.
